shared_topics.title: Trump-Iran agreement and the GOP backlash
shared_topics.summary: Trump signed a 14-point agreement at the G7 intended to end the U.S.-Iran war, reopening the Strait of Hormuz and lifting sanctions on Tehran in exchange for terms that include Iran refraining from pursuing a nuclear weapon. Numerous Senate Republicans, including Wicker, Cassidy, Cornyn and Murkowski, publicly questioned the deal and complained they had not been briefed on its details. VP Vance traveled to Switzerland for follow-on talks. The administration is framing it as a peace achievement.
shared_topics.correlation_label: 70 - Both sides report the same deal and the same real GOP unease; left leads with Trump facing his own party, right leads with the demand for a vote and the surrender-vs-peace debate.

left.framing: Coverage centers on the unusual sight of Trump being rebuked by powerful members of his own party. Reporting emphasizes a somber Senate GOP, the secrecy of the terms, and the political risk the deal carries into the midterms.

right.framing: Coverage acknowledges the same GOP criticism but frames it as a debate over substance: hawks who call the secret terms a surrender versus those who credit Trump for ending a war and reopening the Strait. Emphasis falls on Congress demanding a vote and Trump warning Iran of 'ultimate consequences.'

shared_topics.title: Immigration enforcement: $70B funding vs. courtroom losses
shared_topics.summary: House Republicans passed roughly $70 billion in ICE and Border Patrol funding, sending it to Trump's desk and fully funding immigration enforcement for the rest of his term. In the same window, a federal judge struck down an administration policy that had frozen immigration processing for nationals of 39 countries, ordering benefits and naturalizations to resume. Both events were covered across the spectrum, but the chosen emphasis diverged sharply.
shared_topics.correlation_label: 41 - Same two events, near-opposite emphasis: left leads with the court defeat, detainee deaths and cuts to legal immigration; right leads with the funding win and restored enforcement capacity.

left.framing: Coverage foregrounds the judge striking down the processing freeze, the scale of cuts to legal immigration, and scrutiny of ICE ending its policy of reporting recently released detainee deaths.

right.framing: Coverage leads with House Republicans delivering $70B to fully fund ICE and CBP and ending a months-long intra-party fight, treating it as a durable enforcement win rather than centering the court setback.

shared_topics.title: Trump approval and the 2026 midterm outlook
shared_topics.summary: Multiple polls show Trump's overall approval near a second-term low (about 42 percent) and his economic approval lower still, with affordability anger weighing on Republicans. Democrats hold a modest lead on the generic congressional ballot, though the Democratic Party's own brand also sits in negative territory.
shared_topics.correlation_label: 52 - Same polling environment, opposite lead: left highlights Trump's sinking approval and a Democratic edge, right highlights that Democrats are also underwater.

left.framing: Reporting foregrounds Trump's poor marks and a 5-point Democratic edge for control of Congress, tying GOP exposure to economic anger and a career-low economic approval rating.

right.framing: Reporting accepts GOP headwinds but stresses that the Democratic brand has sunk to a new voter low and that both parties are underwater, reframing the story as shared unpopularity rather than a Democratic advantage.

shared_topics.title: Georgia Senate runoff and Trump's endorsement test
shared_topics.summary: Rep. Mike Collins won the Georgia Republican Senate runoff with Trump's backing and will face Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff in a contest that could help decide Senate control. The night was framed as a test of Trump's endorsement power across several Republican primaries, including Rick Jackson's governor-runoff win.
shared_topics.correlation_label: 62 - Same result; right frames it as a clean Trump-endorsement win, left frames it as one of several tests of Trump's sway with a tough general election ahead.

left.framing: Coverage treats the runoff as a data point in a broader question of how much Trump's endorsement still moves Republican primaries, and looks ahead to a competitive Ossoff race.

right.framing: Coverage frames the outcome as a decisive Trump-endorsement victory and a win for the MAGA wing heading into a pivotal 2026 contest.

shared_topics.title: Trump-Meloni feud after the G7
shared_topics.summary: After the G7 summit, Trump repeatedly claimed Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni asked him for a photo, an account Meloni publicly rejected. The exchange surfaced wider tension linked to Italy's posture on the U.S.-Iran conflict.
shared_topics.correlation_label: 78 - Both report the same back-and-forth and Meloni's denial with little factual divergence; difference is mostly tone and word choice (begged vs. asked).

left.framing: Reporting presents Trump doubling down on the claim and Meloni rejecting it, situating the spat within strained relations over Iran.

right.framing: Reporting covers the same exchange and Meloni's pushback, framing it as a growing diplomatic flare-up between two leaders.

gap_left.title: Mamdani rallies progressives against the Democratic establishment
gap_left.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani campaigned with Bernie Sanders and progressive primary challengers, testing his influence within the party and sharply criticizing the Democratic establishment. The coverage appeared only on the left in this window.

gap_left.title: Medicaid and SNAP cuts as a midterm attack line
gap_left.summary: A House budget bill backed by Trump that pairs tax breaks with cuts to Medicaid and SNAP is being cast by Democratic voices as a vote Republicans will pay for at the polls. The framing as a GOP liability ran on the left and was not mirrored on the right in this window.

gap_left.title: ICE detainee deaths and the end of death reporting
gap_left.summary: ICE is ending its practice of reporting the deaths of recently released detainees amid scrutiny that nearly 50 detainees have died since Trump returned to office, with at least 18 in 2026. The accountability angle appeared only on the left in this window.

gap_left.title: Cuts to legal immigration outpace border cuts
gap_left.summary: Analysis cited by left-leaning outlets argues that 2026 reductions to legal immigration are, on a monthly basis, roughly twice as large as the reduction in illegal border crossings, reframing the administration's immigration record as a curb on legal pathways. This framing ran only on the left.

gap_left.title: Minneapolis police shooting during an immigration arrest
gap_left.summary: An officer who shot a woman in Minneapolis was reportedly dragged by a vehicle during a June immigration arrest, a local-enforcement-consequences story that surfaced on the left and was not picked up on the right in this window.

gap_right.title: Platner's Maine primary win and a #MeToo double-standard charge
gap_right.summary: After Graham Platner won a Maine Democratic primary, conservative commentary argued the result shows the left applies an inconsistent standard on candidate conduct and #MeToo. The angle ran only on the right in this window.

gap_right.title: Virginia prosecutors refuse to enforce a new assault-weapons ban
gap_right.summary: Thirteen Republican commonwealth's attorneys in Virginia announced they will not enforce the state's new assault-weapons ban taking effect July 1, calling it unconstitutional. The story appeared only on the right in this window.

gap_right.title: Massie defeated as a Trump-loyalty test in Kentucky
gap_right.summary: Trump-backed Republican Ed Gallrein declared victory over longtime Rep. Thomas Massie in Kentucky, a result the right covered as vindication of Trump's grip on the GOP and a warning to intra-party dissenters. The framing ran on the right in this window.

gap_right.title: Inflation blamed on the Iran war's fuel-cost shock
gap_right.summary: With inflation jumping to 4.2 percent, its highest since early 2023, right-leaning coverage emphasized Iran-war fuel costs as the driver and scrutinized new Fed task forces, framing the spike as externally caused rather than a result of administration policy. This emphasis ran on the right.

gap_right.title: Americanism and the case for immigration restrictionism
gap_right.summary: Conservative outlets ran ideological essays on national identity and who can become American, making the affirmative case for immigration restrictionism as a matter of principle rather than logistics. This thematic coverage appeared only on the right.
